item.title: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye agree to deploy forces in Gulf
item.description: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye have agreed to implement the trilateral defence agreement and “provide the agreed military forces and capabilities and ensure rapid deployment” in the Gulf country ...
item.dc:creator: Agencies
item.content:encoded: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye have agreed to implement the trilateral defence agreement and “provide the agreed military forces and capabilities and ensure rapid deployment” in the Gulf country in the wake of Houthi attacks. The three sides had convened an emergency meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee (SPDC) of the Makkah Alliance for Defence in Riyadh on Monday to address the regional developments and threats facing Saudi Arabia, according to a joint statement. The trilateral defence agreement, signed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye in August, establishes a framework for collective deterrence and stipulates that an armed attack against any one of them would be regarded as an attack against all. The SPDC on Monday reviewed the outcomes of the political and military consultations preceding the meeting and approved the recommendations submitted to it. It affirmed that the Makkah agreement embodies a firm commitment to collective defence and a unified position in confronting threats. The committee “decided to move immediately to the practical implementation of the collective defence commitments and to take the necessary measures to provide the agreed military forces and capabilities and ensure their rapid deployment in the Kingdom”. “The three countries affirmed that the security of each party is an integral part of the collective security of the three countries,” the statement said. The statement did not give any details or schedule of troop deployment. It also did not specifically name the Houthis as a threat, but the development comes against the backdrop of Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. The three sides condemned in the strongest terms the attempted targeting of Makkah and Madinah, as well as the continuing attacks targeting cities and civilian and economic facilities in the Kingdom. As part of the institutional development of the alliance, the committee decided to appoint General Nauman Mahmood (Retdired) of Pakistan as the first Secretary-General for a three-year term. The SPDC meeting was held as Yemen’s Saudi-led coalition government launched a major military campaign on Sunday to recapture territory held by the Houthis. The SPDC is a key organ of the Makkah pact and comprises the foreign ministers, defence ministers and chiefs of army staff of the three members. Last month, the chiefs of defence forces and chiefs of general staff of the three countries met in Riyadh and reviewed the security situation and the threats facing Saudi Arabia. Trump faces flak fot  ‘Iran could take out LA’ remark President Donald Trump suggested to a crowd of his supporters in Nebraska that Iran could “take out” a ??major United States (US) city like Los Angeles or San Diego, drawing a swift rebuke from California’s Democratic leaders and some fellow Republicans. Trump, speaking at a political rally in the state’s farm belt on Monday, discussed American wartime economic sacrifices and said he was determined to “see a tremendous victory, because it verifies all the things we did.” “And again, remember, with the war, it’s just artificial, it’s a little bit high, it’s a small price to pay,” he told the crowd in Grand Island, Nebraska, apparently referring to rising prices of fuel, fertiliser and other products attributed to energy market disruptions from the war. “It’s a small price to pay for keeping the world safe, for keeping our country safe. They could take out a city. Let ‘em take out Los Angeles, let ‘em take out San Diego. This is a very small price to pay, and it’s going to be over with very soon,” he said.  On Tuesday, the White House dismissed criticism of the remark. “He was saying the US is fighting to STOP Iran from having the ability to take out LA and San Diego with a nuclear weapon — which they would if they had the chance,” a White House account posted on X.

item.title: OpenAI in talks with UAE funds, BlackRock for $30 billion funding round
item.description: UAE investment funds have discussed investing as much as $10 billion altogether, while OpenAI is seeking capital at a valuation of about $1.4 trillion ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: By Ed Ludlow, Rebecca Torrence, Shirin Ghaffary and Natasha Mascarenhas OpenAI is in talks with multiple investment funds from the United Arab Emirates, including Abu Dhabi-based MGX, to help anchor a $30 billion round of financing for the ChatGPT maker, according to people familiar with the matter. The funds would form a syndicate to invest in the round, one of the people said. The UAE funds have discussed putting in as much as $10 billion altogether, one person said. BlackRock Inc. is also in discussions to participate in the round alongside that syndicate, the people said. The fundraise is ongoing and the details could change, said the people, requesting anonymity to discuss private information. OpenAI and BlackRock declined to comment. Representatives for MGX did not respond to requests for comment outside normal business hours. OpenAI is looking to raise at least $30 billion in capital at a valuation of about $1.4 trillion, Bloomberg News has reported, as the firm pushes back plans for an initial public offering until at least next year, citing its focus on AI safety efforts. OpenAI most recently raised a $122 billion round in March at an $852 billion valuation, including the money. Top AI firms, including OpenAI and Anthropic PBC, have previously turned to deep-pocketed investors in the Middle East to meet their intense capital needs to develop and support cutting-edge artificial intelligence software. MGX has invested in prior OpenAI and Anthropic rounds. The investment firm raised close to $50 billion earlier this year to accelerate spending on AI infrastructure and technology, Bloomberg News has reported. OpenAI has held talks with the University of California’s endowment fund, an existing investor, about participating in the round, the people said. Existing backers Thrive Capital and Andreessen Horowitz have also discussed putting in money, the people said. Thrive declined to comment. Representatives for Andreessen and the University of California didn’t respond to requests for comment. Unlike typical venture rounds, OpenAI is presenting its $1.4 trillion pre-money valuation to investors as a set price despite not yet settling on a lead investor, the people said. Normally, investment firms submit terms for funding rounds and negotiate with the company about leading it. --With assistance from Alex Dooler

item.title: Kotak, IndusInd, Axis Bank shares jump on strong Q2 business updates
item.description: Lenders report strong credit and deposit growth aided by FCNR(B) inflows, though analysts flag concerns over CASA momentum ...
item.dc:creator: Subrata Panda
item.content:encoded: Shares of Kotak Mahindra Bank, IndusInd Bank and Axis Bank rose sharply on Tuesday after the lenders reported robust growth in advances and deposits in their quarterly business updates. This growth was aided by healthy mobilisation of FCNR(B) deposits. Kotak Mahindra Bank’s shares jumped 3.59 per cent to close at ₹431.25 on the BSE, while IndusInd Bank gained 2.79 per cent to end at ₹906.95. Axis Bank’s shares rose 2.01 per cent to ₹1,248.50. However, RBL Bank’s shares closed 0.72 per cent lower at ₹414 on the BSE compared with the previous day’s close. On Monday, Kotak Mahindra Bank reported robust net advances (period-end) growth of 25 per cent year-on-year (Y-o-Y) and 13 per cent quarter-on-quarter (Q-o-Q). Excluding advances linked to FCNR(B) deposits, loan growth remained firm at around 21 per cent Y-o-Y and 10 per cent Q-o-Q. Deposits grew 23 per cent Y-o-Y and 14 per cent Q-o-Q, aided by FCNR(B) inflows. Excluding these, deposit growth was more measured at 13 per cent Y-o-Y and 4 per cent Q-o-Q. Current account savings account (CASA) balances grew 11 per cent Y-o-Y and 8 per cent Q-o-Q. The bank mobilised $5.78 billion through FCNR(B) deposits during the quarter. Axis Bank, India’s third-largest private sector lender, said its deposits grew 5.8 per cent sequentially and 20.7 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹14.52 trillion as of September 30, while gross advances rose 8.8 per cent Q-o-Q and 22.7 per cent YoY to ₹13.85 trillion. The lender mobilised $10.62 billion (₹1.02 trillion) in FCNR(B) deposits under the Reserve Bank of India’s swap facility introduced earlier this year.   “While the outcome is good on the loan growth front, the question is sustainability plus core deposit growth around 12-13 per cent for Kotak (Mahindra Bank) and Axis (Bank) isn’t that great. That goes to show that eventually loan growth will have to come down from current levels. CASA growth is also 10 to 11 per cent similar to HDFC Bank showing the pressure that exists in CASA across the system. CASA ratios continue to decline even on core deposit growth basis”, said Suresh Ganapathy, MD&Head - Financial Services Research, Macquarie Capital.  Meanwhile, IndusInd Bank’s net advances grew 11.2 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹3.62 trillion as of September 30, 2026, outpacing the 10.1 per cent growth in deposits to ₹4.29 trillion. IndusInd Bank’s CASA ratio declined to 28 per cent from 30.7 per cent a year earlier and 29.4 per cent in June. The lender mobilised $3.51 billion in FCNR(B) deposits under the RBI’s deposit swap facility, with outstanding loans of about ₹16,564 crore extended from its GIFT City branch against these deposits as of September-end. And, RBL Bank’s total deposits rose 34 per cent Y-o-Y to around ₹1.56 trillion in the quarter ended September 30 (Q2FY27), while gross advances grew 40 per cent to around ₹1.43 trillion. (Disclosure: Entities controlled by the Kotak family have a significant holding in Business Standard Pvt Ltd)

item.title: Google signs massive 3.6-GW power deal with Constellation Energy in US
item.description: The agreements cover 3,590 MW of power, including 890 MW from upgraded nuclear plants, as Constellation plans more than $4.3 billion in new investments ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / Google signs massive 3.6-GW power deal with Constellation Energy in US

Google signs massive 3.6-GW power deal with Constellation Energy in US The agreements cover 3,590 MW of power, including 890 MW from upgraded nuclear plants, as Constellation plans more than $4.3 billion in new investments

Rising electricity demand driven largely by the data centre expansion has contributed to a more than 11-fold increase in PJM capacity prices since 2024 and left the grid with a power shortfall (Photo: Reuters)

Reuters New York 3 min read Last Updated : Oct 06 2026 | 10:24 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Google has contracted for 3,590 megawatts of power from Constellation Energy in the largest US power grid, with new nuclear energy accounting for about a quarter of that supply, the companies said on Tuesday.   Constellation will make more than $4.3 billion of new investments in its fleet as part of the agreement, which involves adding capacity at several of the power company's nuclear reactors in the Midwest and Mid-Atlantic regions, the companies said.   Major tech companies are racing to secure massive amounts of electricity supplies to power data centres across the US by striking unprecedented power deals and reviving the country's nuclear industry.

Over the last two years, Constellation unveiled an agreement to restart its Three Mile Island reactor in Pennsylvania to serve Microsoft data centres, while Google contracted to restart NextEra Energy's nuclear power plant in Iowa.   In the latest arrangement, Google entered into a 20-year power purchase agreement for 890 megawatts of electricity from multiple Constellation-owned nuclear power plants, which would be upgraded to produce more electricity from existing reactors. Electricity from the first of the upgraded plants is expected to be delivered in 2028, the companies said.   Google also entered into a 15-year supply agreement for an additional 2,700 megawatts of power from Constellation in the PJM power grid. That power is not tied to a specific generation source and serves as long-term revenue certainty for Constellation's operating plants, Google said.

Shares of Constellation were up by more than 13 per cent on Tuesday to $304.04 by mid-morning.   Maryland-based Constellation is the largest US nuclear power plant operator and owns a major fleet of natural-gas-fired power plants as well as geothermal energy following its acquisition of electricity producer Calpine Corp earlier this year.   "We're committed to meeting our growth responsibly by actively investing in clean, reliable power that brings new capacity to our nation's grids," said Amanda Peterson Corio, Google's global head of energy and power, in a statement.   The 11 nuclear units expected to be upgraded as part of the arrangement with Google are in Illinois, Pennsylvania, and New Jersey, within the footprint of the largest US electric grid — PJM Interconnection.

Rising electricity demand driven largely by the data centre expansion has contributed to a more than 11-fold increase in PJM capacity prices since 2024 and left the grid with a power shortfall.   In response, PJM management has proposed requiring data centre customers connected to the 13-state grid to either bring their own power or face being shut off from grid power remotely in times of peak demand.   The deal between Google and Constellation is in response to PJM's "bring your own power" proposal. It also creates a "practical model for how major power consumers can expand new supply alongside growing operational requirements, without state or federal mandates," the companies said.

Google and Constellation also agreed on a strategic framework that can be replicated to develop power generation, battery storage, and a flexible power use model known as "demand response" in other parts of the US, the companies said.   Joe Dominguez, chairman, president and CEO of Constellation, said the arrangement with Google is a "model for how technology companies and the energy industry can work together to responsibly develop the digital economy and invest in our nation's energy infrastructure in a way that delivers grid-wide benefits for all, funded by private entities."
